# Jamal — situation → line catalog

**THIS FILE IS THE SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH FOR EVERY STRING THE MOD SPEAKS.** `scripts/lines.lua` and `locale/en/jamaltron.cfg` are GENERATED from it by `tools/gen_lines.py` (PLAN B.5). Both generated files carry a header saying so. **Never hand-edit the generated files** — the next generator run silently eats the edit, and the diff will not tell you which side is right.

Built from [`jamal_profile.md`](jamal_profile.md) and its 125-line verified quote bank, which in turn came from the two per-book profiles. Characterization and every `original` line below are OURS. The book text itself never leaves the gitignored `extracts/`.

## Copyright posture (chotchki's locked call, SPEC.md)

Verbatim lines are **short single-sentence-or-less utterances of one character**, gathered under the non-commercial fan-work fair-use call. No scene, paragraph or exchange is reproduced anywhere. **B.4 IS NOW LOCKED IN FULL (2026-09-19, chotchki), so every `SOURCE: verbatim` row below is a shipping decision rather than a candidate flag.** Two of the rulings have copyright or distribution consequences: the player is *Mr. Engineer* and every Dungeon Crawler Carl proper noun is out of the `Line` column (Q1/Q5 — the ruling that created the third `SOURCE` tag below), and **the one profanity line is CUT** (Q2), so no shipping string in this file contains profanity and the mod portal page needs no content note.

**Every line marked `verbatim` in this file has been machine-verified as an exact substring of the matching extract** (103 distinct strings across 157 rows, plus every full quote quoted in a `Note` cell and every `ORIGINAL:` quote standing behind an `adapted` row; all exact, zero fabrications). Re-verify before B.5 generates anything — a miss is a fabrication and gets deleted, not fixed:

```sh
cd character/extracts && grep -qF -- "<the line>" book7_jamal.txt   # or book8_jamal.txt
```

**Trimmed lines are still verbatim, because every trim is a CONTIGUOUS substring** — a prefix, a suffix, or a whole inner clause. Nothing was cut out of the middle and stitched back together, because that produces a sentence he never said while still passing a careless eyeball check. The `Note` column carries the full quote wherever a trim exists.

**`adapted` is the third provenance tag and it exists for exactly one move: a real quote whose PERSON-REFERENCE we changed.** Chotchki's B.4 Q1/Q5 ruling swaps the book's addressee for *Mr. Engineer*, and at `repaired.08` drops a third-party attribution that has nobody left to point at. Such a line is neither of the other two tags — calling it `original` claims we wrote it, calling it `verbatim` lies to the fidelity checker. So: **`adapted` means the provenance is a real quote, the ONLY thing changed is the person-reference, and the untouched original is recorded in the `Note` cell behind the literal marker `ORIGINAL:` in straight double quotes.**

**STRAIGHT DOUBLE QUOTES IN A `Note` CELL MEAN PROVENANCE AND NOTHING ELSE**, and the voice-editor pass made that a rule rather than a habit. They appear behind `ORIGINAL:` and behind `TRIMMED (…) of`, both of which name a string that came out of a book. **Every other quoted string in a `Note` — a proposed trim, a row this file used to carry, a phrase under discussion — is in *italics*, which is what the prose already does everywhere else.** Two `Note` cells were putting a PROPOSED trim in straight doubles (`flopping.38`, `jump_refused.19`); a checker that greps straight-quoted strings and validates them against the extracts would have been fed a string this file invented, and it only passed because both trims happen to be substrings of their own verbatim rows. Fixed in place. That marker is a machine contract, not decoration — the checker greps it and validates the source line exactly as it validates a `verbatim` row, so an adapted row stays as traceable as the day it was a quote. 14 rows carry it. Everything in the paragraph below still applies to every word around the swapped name.

**Smoothing a quote is fabricating it.** His double plurals (*sticky feets*), his ellipses, his em-dash interruption, his curly apostrophes and his trailing dialogue-tag commas are the signal, and they are reproduced character for character. Where a line reads like a fragment (`Gentlemen,` / `I must give you an apology`) that is because the book punctuates it that way.

## How to read the table (the machine contract for B.5)

Every section is `## <event>`, then a `key:` line naming the Lua table key, then a `split:` line, then a `fires:` note, then ONE table with these **twelve** columns in this order:

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ID` | stable, unique across the whole file. Becomes the locale key `jamaltron-line.<id>`. Never renumber an ID that has shipped |
| `Line` | the string, exactly as it should render. **Every row has one** — there is no longer any such thing as a pool entry with no string (see the channels section) |
| `CH` | `speech` \| `narration` — **which of the mod's two output channels this row goes to.** The most load-bearing column in the table; see the channels section immediately below |
| `SOURCE` | `verbatim` (exact substring of an extract), `adapted` (a real quote with only the person-reference changed; the untouched original sits in `Note` behind `ORIGINAL:`), or `original` (written by us in his voice). **Load-bearing — do not blur these** |
| `BK` | `7` or `8` for verbatim, `-` for original |
| `W` | integer relative weight WITHIN this pool. Not a probability, not normalized — the picker sums the eligible rows and rolls |
| `TIER` | `quiet` \| `normal` \| `unbearable` |
| `SUB` | subpool, condition, advisory tag, or `-`/`any`. **What it MEANS is set by the section's `split:` line, never inferred from this column** — three incompatible meanings share this cell and only the `split:` line separates them; see below |
| `GATE` | `-` or `once_per_save` — a hard once-per-entity-per-save eligibility gate, orthogonal to `W` and `TIER`. 9 rows carry it; see the gate section |
| `CHAIN` | `-`, or `<row id>@<ticks>` on a SETUP row, or `tail` / `tail-only` on the follow-up it names. Newest column; the full contract is in the chaining section below |
| `GRP` | anti-repeat group: the ID of the FIRST row in this file carrying that exact `Line`. A unique string is its own group. **Computed, never hand-assigned.** D.5 keys anti-repeat on this, per ENTITY, across pools |
| `Note` | why the line is here, the full quote when trimmed, the `ORIGINAL:` quote when adapted, and the B.4 ruling where one applies |

**IDs were renumbered twice, both on 2026-09-19, and that door is now CLOSED.** Renumbering was legal for exactly one reason: **nothing references these ids yet** — `scripts/lines.lua` and `locale/en/jamaltron.cfg` do not exist until B.5 generates them. **The moment B.5 runs, an id becomes a locale key, a locale key is a public contract, and a cut row leaves a GAP whose id is retired forever.**

- **Pass 1, the Q5 proper-noun purge, cut three rows.** `command_done`'s two were the tail of its own pool so it simply got shorter; OLD `idle.25` was mid-pool, so `idle` was renumbered — old `idle.26`–`.39` became `idle.25`–`.38`. **`idle.25` therefore names two different rows depending on which side of this pass you are reading, and pass 3 has now retired the second one. That is the whole case against renumbering in one id**, and it is why the pass-3 cuts left gaps instead.
- **Pass 2, the B.4 cuts, cut six rows** (Q2, Q3 and Q12). Four were pool tails and cost nothing: `attacking.15`, `jump.14`, `legs_break.33`, `flopping.42`. Two were mid-pool, so both pools were renumbered: `damaged` old `.09`–`.16` are now `.08`–`.15`, and `flopping` old `.38`–`.41` are now `.37`–`.40`.
- **Pass 3, the voice-audit cuts, cut three rows — AND THIS IS THE PASS THAT LEFT GAPS, ON PURPOSE.** `idle.24` and `jump_refused.18` (one string, *You need to remain in the garage.*, reused in two pools: it reads as Jamal ORDERING the engineer, which he never does, into a garage Factorio does not have) and `idle.25` (*He’s still very sad about his friends.* — social reporting with no possible referent in single-player). **Nothing was renumbered and nothing will be.** `idle` now runs `.01`–`.23` then `.26`–`.38`, `jump_refused` skips `.18`, and those three ids are retired. This is the door in the paragraph above working as designed rather than an exception to it.
- **Pass 5, the voice-editor pass, cut ten rows and renumbered nothing.** `enter.08`, `exit.06`, `idle.33`, `idle.38`, `attacking.14`, `damaged.14`, `low_health.09`, `flopping.05`, `flopping.31`, `command_done.06` — ten more retired ids, each with its reason in the section it left. It also rewrote thirteen `Line` cells, re-trimmed one (`jump.08`), flipped one chain target from `tail` to `tail-only` (`land.04`) and **wrote no new rows at all.** `damaged.15` survives with a rewritten string while `damaged.14` is retired, so `damaged` runs `.01`–`.13` then `.15`.
- **Pass 4, the structural pass, cut one row and renumbered nothing.** `jump_refused.15` (*It is quite thoroughly gone... Just like his ability to hop.* — the `idle.22` string in a pool that cannot supply the *It* the sentence needs; the reasoning is in that section). **`jump_refused` now skips `.15` AND `.18`.** The pass also added the `SUB` conditions for B.6, the `CHAIN` column for B.7, and one re-trim at `idle.20` — a `Line` edit, not an id edit, which is the only kind of surgery this file has left.

**Every in-file cross-reference moved with the rows both times, and that is the step that bites.** Pass 1 shipped with a stale id range that had to be hand-fixed afterwards; pass 2's movers were `flopping.39` → `flopping.38` (the over-cap row, referenced from the length note and from Q8) and `flopping.41` → `flopping.40` (referenced twice from the Q5 swap list). **If a third renumber is ever proposed, the answer is no** — it is now cheaper to live with a gap than to re-audit the references.

### The two output channels — `CH` (chotchki's B.4 ruling, and it is structural)

**The mod has TWO output channels, not one.** `CH` says which one a row belongs to, and it is the first thing a generator should read after `Line`.

- **`speech` — Jamal talking.** Renders as a speech bubble over the entity. **Strict register:** he puts himself in the SUBJECT slot (`Jamal is <verb>ing`), the honorific never drops, and there is no irony and no wordplay outside his own malapropisms. **251 rows.**
- **`narration` — the GAME describing him.** Third person, ABOUT him rather than BY him, and **this is where the books' own narration voice legitimately lives** — the dry aside, the footfall onomatopoeia, the flagged silence. Renders as something visibly not a bubble (floating text or a chat line; D.5 picks). **12 rows.**

**One column, two findings closed, which is why chotchki's framing beats the six separate fixes it replaced.** The rows a voice audit flagged as *off-voice narrator syntax* — `moving.03` *Clack, clack, clack go Jamal's feet.*, `jump.04` *Up goes Jamal!*, `land.08` — were never off-voice. **They were in the WRONG CHANNEL.** A fronted verb makes him the OBJECT of a sportscast, which is wrong in his mouth and exactly right in the narrator's, and the footfall onomatopoeia is the book's narrator looking at him from outside in the first place. Nothing needed cutting; three rows needed moving. **The later voice audit found the ruling had under-applied itself** — two more rows sat in the wrong channel on the identical diagnosis (`flopping.23`, whose own Note called it a caption, and `moving.11`, which uses the narration's *whir* in the pool `moving.03` had just been moved out of), and `died.08` is mis-channelled for a different reason: a past-tense verdict on his whole self is an EPITAPH, and only a survivor utters one.

**AND A CHANNEL MOVE IS NOT A REWRITE, which is what the voice-editor pass had to fix next.** `flopping.23` *Jamal waves his head about most miserably.* and `moving.11` *Jamal's legs are whirring most robustly.* were both `Jamal <verbs> most <adverb>` — ***most* is his #2 lexical marker and third-person-by-name is his backbone**, so once they were re-labelled `narration` the file was shipping a narrator who talks exactly like Jamal, which is worse than the mis-routing was: it makes the channel distinction inaudible at the two pools where it renders most often. **Both were rewritten into an actual narrator register** — flat outside-in observation plus a dry gloss, the shape `low_health.01` and `land.08` already use, with none of his markers in them. The narrator also gets to use a PRONOUN for Jamal, which is the cleanest audible split available: **the name is his, the pronoun is the narrator's.** `moving.11` now lands the book's own joke on top — he was built to be quiet as well as quick, and he audibly is not. And `[SILENCE]` stops meaning *emit nothing* and becomes a narration note, which is the other half of the same ruling.

**B.5 emits `CH` per row and D.5 renders on it.** A generator that flattens the channel ships twelve rows as Jamal saying things about himself in a voice he demonstrably does not have — the exact failure the audit caught, reintroduced by the tooling.

**The `split:` line is the whole `SUB` contract, and it still has exactly three values.** `SUB` is overloaded on purpose — three incompatible meanings in one column — so the `split:` line is what disambiguates them, and a generator MUST read it before it reads the table:

- `none` — every row is in one pool. Any non-`-` `SUB` here is an ADVISORY tag for B.4 (`sincere`, `meta`); it changes nothing about the roll. **9 of the 15 sections.**
- `required — a | b` — a real fork. The mod knows which side fired before it rolls, and rolls inside that side only, and EVERY row picks a side. Two sections: `enter/exit` and `legs break`.
- `gated — <dimension>: <value> | <value> | ...` — **conditional eligibility, and this is the one that grew.** The mod reports a condition at fire time; a row tagged `any` is always eligible, a row tagged with a value is eligible only when the mod reports exactly that value, and **a value the mod cannot report matches nothing, so its rows never roll.** Four sections: `attacking` (`friendly`), `jump refused` (`reason`, B.6), `land` (`outcome`), `flopping` (`fork`).

**`gated` generalized from one tag to a named dimension at the structural pass, and the old spelling still stands.** `attacking` predates the generalization and writes its always-eligible rows as `-` rather than `any`: **in a `gated` section `-` and `any` mean the same thing**, and the three new sections spell it `any` so that a classification is visibly a DECISION rather than an omission. A generator needs one line for this and nothing else changes.

**Why `gated` and not `required` for the three new ones.** A required fork makes every row pick a side, and in all three sections most rows are condition-agnostic — a lament works whoever broke the legs, a grievance about the arc works whether or not a cliff was in the way. Forcing them to a side would halve each pool for no gain and push several tier cells under the four-string floor. `gated` keeps the agnostic rows in both rolls and reserves the tag for rows that would LIE under the wrong condition, which is the only thing the split is actually for.

**Three of the four `gated` dimensions are currently under-reported by the mod, and that is the safe direction.** `attacking`'s `friendly` waits on the API (Q11), `jump refused`'s `reason` waits on E.2, `land`'s `outcome` waits on the E.3/E.4 reorder and `flopping`'s `fork` waits on D.5 storing it. **Until each lands, the tagged rows sit out and the `any` rows carry the pool** — the mod is quieter than designed, never wronger.

**A generator that treats every non-`-` `SUB` as a fork silently breaks three pools** — it would make `idle`'s four weight-1 sincere lines a coin flip against the other 32 rows, and it would make `jump.13`, the single surviving `meta` row, either half of all jumps or unreachable. This paragraph exists because that is the single easiest way to get B.5 wrong. **Note that `SUB = sincere` is now doubly advisory:** those rows are gated by the `GATE` column, not by `SUB`, so a generator that ignores `SUB` entirely on a `split: none` section is CORRECT and one that forks on it is wrong twice. **It survives on six rows and no longer on `jump_refused.20`**, where B.6's real `reason` split took the column over — nothing was lost, because the nine gated rows are enumerated by ID below and the tag never drove anything.

**Tiers are CUMULATIVE.** `quiet` plays quiet only. `normal` plays quiet + normal. `unbearable` plays everything. So a `quiet` line is not a quiet line, it is a line good enough to survive a friend opting mostly out — those are the best ones, and `unbearable` is where the apology spam lives.

**Tiers key off REGISTER, not just volume** — this is the profile's most machinable finding and the one most likely to get flattened by accident. His escalation is INVERTED: formality is inversely proportional to actual severity, so the routine events get the baroque politeness and the rare serious events get the plain short words. A tier system that only prunes frequency loses the joke.

**Tokens** (the generator substitutes, the locale file uses `__1__` style parameters):

- `{PLAYER}` — **GONE. RESOLVED 2026-09-19 (chotchki): the player is *Mr. Engineer*, and the literal string is baked into all 26 rows that carried the token.** Reason: Factorio's engineer is canonically NAMELESS — that is Wube's own position, so there is no real name to use — and Jamal's honorific tic is about the FORM, not the name: *Mister* / *Mr.* / *Miss* + given name, never dropped, applied to literally everyone including a pet dinosaur. *Mr. Engineer* satisfies the form and is canonical Factorio. **Baked rather than left as a token because there is no per-player variance left to represent**, and baking it makes the authored character counts in this file TRUE — B.5 substitutes nothing and re-measures nothing. *Gentlemen* stays where the book used it (`legs_break.32`, `flopping.25`), because he addresses groups that way regardless of who is actually present.
- `{N}` — this entity's cumulative leg-break count. **SHIPS (B.4 Q9).** Both books count hardware out loud and book 7 counts it in protest; the mod already knows the number, so the gag gets better every time it fires. **Cheapest high-value feature in the character.** 4 rows use it — `legs_break.17`, `legs_break.27`, `flopping.30`, `repaired.06` — and they top out at **51** characters even with a three-digit count (`repaired.06`).

  **Storage cost, stated precisely so E.6 can price it:** `{N}` needs `storage`-only per-entity state, which E.6 already requires for multiplayer sync, so this is a table keyed by `unit_number` holding an integer — plus, in the same table, the `once_per_save` fired-set the `GATE` column needs. **No mutable module-level state, no per-tick work, one entry per jamaltron.** The entry is created lazily on the first break and removed on `on_entity_died` / `on_object_destroyed`, or it leaks one small record per destroyed entity for the life of the save.

**`[SILENCE]` IS GONE. The six silence rows are now NARRATION rows with real strings (B.4 Q7).** The old encoding was *the picker selects this row and emits nothing*, and it was wrong twice over: a speech mod is structurally bad at silence, and an emitted absence is indistinguishable from a mod that failed to fire. **In both books his going quiet is how the text says something is badly wrong, and both narrations FLAG it as the anomaly** — so the mod flags it too, in the channel built for exactly that.

chotchki's wording for the shape is *Jamal is silent... for once*. **Each of the six carries its own per-pool wording rather than that one string six times**, because a silence at `died` and a silence at `low_health` are not the same moment even though the books use his silence as the distress signal in both:

| Row | String | The moment |
|---|---|---|
| `attacking.03` | Jamal has stopped apologizing. Jamal is feeding. | bk 7's berserker frenzy switches the manners off entirely |
| `damaged.02` | Jamal makes a noise that is not a word. | damage is a NOISE in both books, never a sentence |
| `low_health.01` | Jamal has gone quiet. That is never a good sign. | the distress signal — still deliberately the heaviest row in the file |
| `legs_break.18` | The legs come apart. Jamal says nothing at all. | bk 8's break is wordless; the event happens and he says nothing |
| `repaired.13` | Jamal is silent... for once. | the contented come-down, and the one pool that earns the dry *for once* |
| `died.01` | Jamal does not get up. | mercy. Nobody in two books is ever cruel to him, so no punchline |

All six are `SOURCE = original`, `BK = -`, `CH = narration`, at their previous weights and tiers. `died.01` reads *Jamal does not get up.* rather than *Jamal is quiet now.* since the voice audit — see below.

**THE PREFIX SHIPS, AND D.5 APPLIES IT AT RENDER TIME.** chotchki's Q7 wording specified the encoding literally — *Game Note: <Jamal is silent ... for once>* — and this file recorded the comment, dropped the prefix and deferred to D.5 without recording that it had deferred anything. That is how a stated encoding goes missing. **So, decided and written down: every `narration` row renders as `Game Note: ` + the row's string, and the prefix lives in the RENDERER, not in the `Line` column.** One place instead of twelve, because twelve cells is twelve chances to typo the same eleven characters; the length cap and the fidelity checker should measure the string we actually authored and nothing else; and a wrapper D.5 owns changes once, in one file, when chotchki looks at real floating text in-game.

Two consequences, stated rather than discovered later:

- **The ≤ 60 cap is a speech-BUBBLE constraint and narration does not render in a bubble**, so the wrapper costs nothing against it. D.5's own width budget is the longest narration string plus the wrapper: **49 + 11 = 60 characters** today (`flopping.23`, after the voice-editor rewrite; `low_health.01` and `attacking.03` tie one behind it at 48).
- **The angle brackets are read as chotchki's placeholder notation for the row's string, not as literal characters to print.** That is the one interpretation call in this ruling, it is flagged here rather than buried, and it is cheap to flip — one line here and one line in D.5 — if he wants the brackets rendered.

**THREE OF THESE ROWS ASSERT AN ONGOING SILENCE, AND A NAMED SILENCE THE MOD BREAKS INSIDE A TICK IS A SHRUG.** The profile's version of him going quiet is a SUSTAINED absence — hours hanging off a ceiling saying nothing, a whole feeding frenzy, a wordless break — and naming the silence and then talking straight over it is worse than never naming it, because the player learns the narration lies. **D.5 MUST HONOUR A SUPPRESSION WINDOW on these three.** Each has a boundary the mod already computes, so this is bookkeeping and not a new subsystem:

| Row | The window | The boundary the mod already has |
|---|---|---|
| `attacking.03` | the rest of the current combat burst | the `attacking` throttle — no row fires again until the gun has been quiet long enough to re-arm the pool |
| `legs_break.18` | the first `flopping` interval | the apology timer's first tick is skipped, which is also bk 8's actual beat: the break, and only then the flopping |
| `low_health.01` | 15 s of `speech` on that entity (suggested — A.7 can tune it against a real bubble) | one timestamp per entity, in the same `storage` record as `{N}` and the `once_per_save` fired-set |

**Scope, so nobody has to guess at it:** the window is per ENTITY, it suppresses the `speech` channel only (the narrator is not him, so narration still fires), and it SUPPRESSES rather than re-rolls — emitting a second-choice line is the exact failure this ruling exists to prevent. **It gates BEFORE the roll, which is the detail that keeps the paragraph below true:** the picker still has no emit-nothing branch, because a suppressed event never reaches the picker at all. **`damaged.02`, `repaired.13` and `died.01` need no window and ship as they are:** a noise is not a silence, a wreck has nothing left to contradict it, and the come-down at `repaired.13` is the only one of the three that could earn a window later, if in-game the bubble after it reads as the mod stepping on its own beat.

**This changes the Lua shape B.5 emits**, and in the simplifying direction: there is no longer a pool entry with no string, so the generator has no absent-string branch at all and D.5's picker has no "emit nothing" path to get wrong. The only new conditional is which channel to render in.

**Line length.** Hard target ≤ 60 characters — it renders over a walking vehicle in a Factorio speech bubble. Two shipped lines sit slightly over (61 and 64) and are flagged in place with a trim offered; everything else fits. Median line length here is 38 characters, which matches him: his median usable utterance across two books is 5–9 words.

**The cap is now measured on the SHIPPING string, because there is nothing left to substitute into it.** Baking *Mr. Engineer* in killed the old caveat: the token was 8 characters and the literal is 12, and at that width the longest affected row is `legs_break.20` at **60**, exactly on the cap, with `repaired.03` and `repaired.16` behind it at 58. (The header said 58 was the ceiling until the voice-editor pass recomputed it — `legs_break.20` picked the honorific up in a rewrite AFTER that number was measured, which is how a computed number goes stale without anybody editing it.) **Zero rows cross 60 as a result of the bake, so the authored lengths in this file are the real lengths and B.5 does not have to re-measure** (the two rows that were already over are below). The only token left is `{N}`, 1–3 characters, and the four rows carrying it top out at **51** even with a three-digit count (`legs_break.17` 47, `legs_break.27` 50, `flopping.30` 49, `repaired.06` 51). **The two rows over the cap (`flopping.38` at 61, `jump_refused.19` at 64) stay UNTRIMMED, by ruling (B.4 Q8).** They were over before any of this, both have a trim written into their `Note` cell, and neither trim gets taken on a guess — **chotchki measures a real speech bubble in-game at A.7 and the number decides.** Trimming now would spend *reverse psychologicalize*, his best malaprop, to satisfy a cap nobody has verified exists at 60. These two are also the only over-cap rows this file will ever have: *Mr. Engineer* is baked in, the longest row it touches lands at 58, and `{N}` tops out at 51.

## Anti-repeat — the `GRP` contract (B.4 Q13, locked)

**Anti-repeat keys on `GRP`, per ENTITY, ACROSS pools. Not on `ID`, and not per pool.** 205 distinct strings fill 263 rows and **45 of those strings live in more than one pool, occupying 103 rows**, so per-pool suppression is blind precisely where it matters most: `legs break` and `flopping` fire back to back — the break, then the apology timer — and **they share 16 strings.** A per-pool suppressor cannot see that `flopping` is about to re-say the break line the player read two seconds ago, at the mod's centerpiece moment. Same shape, smaller, for `built` ∩ `repaired` (6 shared), and *Jamal must protest!* / *Nothing is wrong.* each span four pools.

`GRP` is **the ID of the FIRST row in this file carrying that exact `Line`**; a row whose string is unique is its own group. **It is computed, never hand-assigned** — hand-assignment is how the same sentence lands in two groups and the mechanism silently stops working while still looking correct in review.

**The locale file is NOT deduplicated: one key per `ID`, always.** It costs a few hundred bytes, it keeps ID→key total, and it leaves a reused line free to diverge per pool later. **`GRP` is for the picker, `ID` is for the locale**, and conflating them is the one way to get this wrong in both directions at once.

**One canonical exception, recorded as an explicit allow-list.** `idle.01` → `idle.02` is the same observation said once and then repeated later verbatim with *indeed* bolted on; he is the only character in the books who quotes himself, and a system allowed to repeat that one succession reproduces a gag he performs on himself. Two honest notes on it: the pair is two different strings and therefore two different groups, so **a strictly group-keyed suppressor already permits it** — the allow-list exists so a later near-duplicate heuristic cannot silently kill the gag. And record it as an **ordered** pair, not a symmetric one: the callback only works in that direction.

**That old hook is now CLOSED: `idle.01` → `idle.02` does NOT become a `CHAIN`, and the chaining mechanism is the reason it should not.** In the book the callback lands CHAPTERS later, and the joke is that he is still pleased with a line nobody else remembers. A chain fires the second beat on a two-second timer, which converts a surprise callback into a stutter. **Permitted-but-not-scheduled is the correct encoding and it always was** — the allow-list stays, the `CHAIN` cells on both rows stay `-`.

**Chain follow-ups are EXEMPT from everything in this section.** A `tail` delivered by its head does not consult `GRP`, does not respect the suppression window and does not touch the cooldown — the pair is one utterance in two beats and only the HEAD is a new utterance. A follow-up that the picker rolls INDEPENDENTLY (a `tail`, never a `tail-only`) is an ordinary pick and gets the ordinary treatment.

### `GATE = once_per_save` (B.4 Q6, locked)

**Seven sincere/identity rows are gated to once per entity per save, at their existing tiers and weights, unchanged:** `idle.34`, `idle.35`, `low_health.10`–`.13`, `jump_refused.20`.

**It was NINE until the voice-editor pass cut `idle.33` and `idle.38`**, the two gated rows whose trims did not parse — `idle.33` opened on a bare *he* for himself, which inverts his strongest tic, and `idle.38` needed the *It's what* it had been cut away from to supply the object of *do*. Neither had a contiguous re-cut that fixed it and neither full quote fits a bubble (82 and 66 characters), so both are retired. **The `idle` sincere beats that survive are the fear (`idle.34`) and the identity line (`idle.35`); the ocean beat is gone**, and that is a real loss recorded rather than papered over — the trigger table names the ocean as one of the two things this pool owes. Writing a replacement would mean inventing the one register in two books where he stops being funny, so nothing was written.

**Weight 1 was never a rarity mechanism, and that is the whole argument.** Tiers are cumulative and weights are relative WITHIN the eligible set, so tagging a row `quiet` SHRINKS the pool it competes in — which means a `quiet`-tagged weight-1 row is roughly **3.6x MORE likely to fire for the player who asked for the least Jamal than for the player who asked for the most.** The arithmetic is under `idle`. Weight 1 was not rare, it was just quiet, and no tier or weight can fix an inversion that tiers and weights created.

A hard gate can. **`once_per_save` makes the identity material land as a MOMENT instead of a rotation** — the one thing it has to do, because it is the only place in two books where he stops being funny. D.5 stores the fired-set per entity in `storage`, in the same record as `{N}`, so the mechanism costs nothing it was not already paying for.

## Line chaining — the `CHAIN` contract (B.4 answer #14, semantics LOCKED in SPEC.md)

**Some rows in this file only parse after a partner line, and `GRP` anti-repeat actively works against delivering one.** *I have, I mean.* corrects a *Jamal* that has to have been said first. *How many lemurs?* is a follow-up question to a question. *Jamal is giving you all of them.* has no antecedent for *them*. The catalog has carried the problem since B.3 with no mechanism to answer it; **B.7 adds the column, and every semantic below is chotchki's, transcribed from SPEC.md rather than invented here.**

**B.7 named nine rows and the count was wrong in both directions, which is worth recording because it is the kind of error a list of ids hides.** `flopping.21` is a tenth orphan with the identical defect and was missed because it is a REUSED string — its `Note` lives at `legs_break.12`, so the row that carried the problem carried no note about it. And `jump.08` is not an orphan this mechanism can fix: its partner is one EVENT away, not one delay away. **Nine chains ship. They are not the nine rows the plan listed.**

**The column grammar**, which is the whole machine contract:

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `-` | not part of any chain. 245 rows |
| `<row id>@<ticks>` | **HEAD.** When this row fires, schedule that row on the same entity after that many ticks. The target is always in the SAME pool |
| `tail` | **FOLLOW-UP that also stands alone.** A head names it; the picker may also roll it normally |
| `tail-only` | **FOLLOW-UP that does not stand alone.** The picker MUST exclude it from every ordinary roll. Miss this and the punchline fires by itself, which is worse than not having the pair at all |

**One hop only**, so a `tail` is never also a head and the grammar cannot express a three-beat gag. A walking vehicle does not hold an audience for three beats.

**The rest of the semantics, verbatim in force from SPEC.md:** the follow-up is **EXEMPT from anti-repeat, from the `GRP` suppression window and from the say-cooldown** — those gate new utterances and the punchline is not one, it is the second half of the utterance already in flight. It **inherits the HEAD's tier**, so a `normal` follow-up behind a `quiet` head plays for a `quiet` player and the `TIER` cell on a `tail-only` row is advisory only; gating it at its own tier would fire setups whose punchline is silently dropped. It is **CANCELLED if the entity dies, is swapped (D.4, including the beached swap) or is mined** before it fires — a punchline delivered by a corpse is a bug. Pending chains live in the same per-entity `storage` table as `{N}`, the `once_per_save` fired-set and the `flopping` fork.

**The delay is COMPUTED, not taste.** Every value here is `3.5 ticks per character of the HEAD's string, rounded to the nearest 30, floor 60` — long enough that the first bubble can be read, short enough that the two beats are one utterance. **B.5 should recompute it from the head rather than copying the number**, the same way `GRP` is computed rather than hand-assigned; a hand-tuned delay is a number nobody can re-derive after the head gets re-trimmed. (`idle.20` got re-trimmed in this very pass, and its delay moved with it.)

**The nine chains:**

| Head | Follow-up | Delay | The beat |
|---|---|---|---|
| `idle.08` | `idle.09` `tail-only` | 150 | *how many clowns I have consumed?* → *How many lemurs?* — the follow-up question, and it is nothing alone |
| `idle.10` | `idle.36` `tail-only` | 120 | *a great yearning Jamal has.* → *I have, I mean.* — **the self-correction, the character's signature tic, and it cannot exist without the row it corrects** |
| `idle.18` | `idle.19` `tail` | 120 | *I suspect it's quite unpleasant.* → *Quite unpleasant indeed.* — the doubling. `tail`, not `tail-only`: *indeed* bolted onto a flat observation is a shape he uses standalone all the time (`idle.05`) |
| `idle.20` | `idle.21` `tail-only` | 180 | the sense-of-smell loss → *Not even one little bit.* **The head was RE-TRIMMED in this pass to stop orphaning it** — see the row |
| `jump_refused.16` | `jump_refused.17` `tail` | 60 | *I cannot reach!* → *I am quite snug!* — the bk 8 wedged pair, back to back in the book, and now both gated to `blocked` where they are funniest. `tail`, because *quite snug* is a complete joke on its own |
| `legs_break.05` | `legs_break.12` `tail-only` | 120 | *so many sorries to give* → *Jamal is giving you all of them.* — **one book sentence, split at the comma.** *them* has no referent without the head |
| `flopping.11` | `flopping.21` `tail-only` | 120 | the same pair, in the pool that reuses both halves. **B.7 named nine rows and this is the tenth — `flopping.21` is the identical orphan and was missed because it is a reused string** |
| `land.11` | `land.04` `tail-only` | 150 | *quite pleased with that landing.* → *he always falls down again.* — the honest downgrade, one sentence later, and the head supplies the *Jamal* that *he* points at. **`tail` → `tail-only` at the voice-editor pass:** rolled alone the follow-up is a bare *he* for himself, which is the tic inverted, and no re-cut can fix it because *Jamal* lives only at the front of the sentence. The head is the only thing that can supply the subject, so the head is now the only thing that fires it |
| `moving.10` | `moving.13` `tail-only` | 120 | *I will attempt driving with my legs.* → *Maybe my mouth.* — the book's own next line. **`attacking.14` carried the same string with no head at all and was CUT at the voice-editor pass**, so this chain is now the fragment's only home: *Maybe* answers a question, and a combat pool never asks one |

**`jump.08` is the one row of B.7's nine that did NOT get a chain, and the reason is structural rather than editorial.** It and `land.04` *he always falls down again.* are two halves of one book sentence, deliberately split across the two EVENTS that sentence describes. Nothing in `jump` can set it up, and a chain to `land.04` would have to span the arc: **the gap between takeoff and touchdown is ~30 ticks of a distance-dependent animation, not a fixed tick delay, and the break roll cancels the pending follow-up in exactly the case the pair is about.** So it stays an independently rollable row — **and the voice-editor pass had to pay for that by RE-TRIMMING it.** The old cut opened on *he doesn't have time to see how high he is*, and the note defending it said a bubble of Jamal saying *he* is Jamal talking about himself. That is exactly backwards: **his third person is his own NAME, and the profile spells the negative out — not *he*, *Jamal*.** A rollable row has to carry its own subject, so `jump.08` now takes the whole prefix, *When Jamal jumps,* included, at 60 characters. `land.04` cannot do the same, because the name is not on its side of the sentence — which is why it went `tail-only` instead. **Same defect, two different fixes, decided by where the noun sits.**

**The tail/tail-only split is now 2 and 7:** `idle.19` and `jump_refused.17` stand alone; `moving.13`, `idle.09`, `idle.21`, `idle.36`, `land.04`, `legs_break.12` and `flopping.21` do not.

## Requirements the catalog cannot enforce

**Two defects found at the structural pass are ORDERING and STATE bugs, not line bugs.** A column can mark the rows that would lie, but only the mod can decide when to roll and what to carry, so both are written down here as requirements against the phase that owns them. **Both were live defects in the shipping catalog, not hypotheticals.**

| # | Owner | Requirement |
|---|---|---|
| **R1** | **E.3 / E.4** | **The leg-break roll MUST resolve before the `land` line is picked**, and its outcome MUST be passed to the picker as the `outcome` condition. Until this pass the pool fired first and asserted a result it could not know — half the `quiet` weight told the player the legs held, on the landing that broke them. **Recommended on top of the ordering:** on a break, `land` does not speak at all — `legs_break` is the landing line — because two bubbles in one tick step on the mod's centerpiece and because a broken landing leaves `land` two eligible strings at `quiet`. See the `land` section |
| **R2** | **D.5** | **The `flopping` pool MUST be rolled with the fork the `legs_break` event carried.** Stamp `self` / `external` on the entity at break time, read it on every apology tick, clear it at `repaired`. Without it the apology timer erases a fork the mod spent a `quiet`-tier row announcing (`legs_break.25`) inside one interval, because **43% of `flopping`'s rollable weight (76 of 178) is the apology register** and the external fork's whole definition is that he does not apologize — at 43% a player hears one inside the first three intervals **81%** of the time. One more field in the per-entity `storage` record that already holds `{N}`, the fired-set and the pending chains. See the `flopping` section |

**Neither requirement can be checked by re-parsing this file**, which is why they are stated as prose with an owner and not encoded as a column. The columns do the half they can: `land`'s `outcome` sub means a mis-ordered picker still cannot choose a row that lies, and `flopping`'s `fork` sub means an un-stamped entity falls back to the `any` rows rather than to the wrong ones.

## enter/exit

**key:** `enter` and `exit` — ONE section because PLAN B.3 names the event that way, TWO pools because the mod fires them separately.
**split:** required — `enter` | `exit`. The mod always knows which of the two fired, so it always knows which subpool to roll. Never pick across them.
**fires:** `on_player_driving_changed_state`. `enter` when a driver mounts, `exit` when they dismount.

**Thin in both books — nobody ever rides him**, so most of this is written fresh. The closest canonical analogue to being mounted is being SUMMONED (he hops off whatever wall he was parked on, delighted), and the analogue to being dismounted is being BENCHED — his flat *What?*, then negotiation, then staying put and sulking.

**Two rows were CUT at the voice-editor pass and both ids are retired.** `enter.08` *Mind the head, Mr. Engineer. It is quite wide.* was **the only imperative to the player in the whole file** — he is permission-seeking, he negotiates rather than obeys, and he never issues an order to anybody; the previous pass cut a VERBATIM row (old `idle.24` / `jump_refused.18`, *You need to remain in the garage.*) for exactly that, so cutting an original for it is not a close call. `exit.06` *Oh, are the others coming back?* is verbatim and still had to go: **“the others” has no referent in a single-player Factorio save**, which is the same test that cut old `idle.25` — a verbatim line with nothing to point at is still a non sequitur (Q5).

## moving

**key:** `moving`
**split:** none
**fires:** driving state changes to moving, or the autopilot/remote picks up a destination. Heavily throttled — this pool can fire constantly, so cooldown does the work, not the weights.

**Thinnest pool in the character.** He is richly DESCRIBED in motion in both books (legs whir, feet click-clack and clank on hard floors, he keeps pace with motorcycles over ten miles) and he almost never narrates it himself. ## idle

**key:** `idle`
**split:** none — `SUB = sincere` is an ADVISORY tag, not a subpool. Those rows sit in the ordinary `idle` roll
**fires:** idle timer while nobody is driving and nothing is happening. The largest pool by a distance and the one a player hears most, so it carries the widest register spread.

**Four of the nine chains live in this pool**, which is not a coincidence: `idle` is the one pool that fires on a bare timer with nothing happening, so it is the only place a two-beat utterance has room to land — and it is where the rows that only parse after a partner accumulated. `idle.08` → `.09`, `idle.10` → `.36`, `idle.18` → `.19`, `idle.20` → `.21`. **Three of those targets are `tail-only` and leave the roll**, which is why this pool's own weight arithmetic below is computed over 103 and not 110.

The profile's most over-anchored event. Note the deliberate inclusion of lines from the sincere monologue at weight 1–2: **the identity material is where he stops being funny, so it is spent rarely and never on a timer alone.** B.4 ruled that it ships, with a `GATE = once_per_save` on each of those rows rather than a trust in weight.

`SUB = sincere` on `idle.34` and `idle.35` is advisory, not a separate pool: they sit in the same `idle` roll at weight 1. **What actually makes them rare is `GATE = once_per_save`, added at B.4, because weight 1 did the OPPOSITE of rare.** Tiers are cumulative and weights are relative WITHIN the eligible set, so tagging a row `quiet` shrinks the pool it competes in. The rollable pool sums to 103 weight (quiet 29 + normal 54 + unbearable 20), so these two are 2 of 29 weight at `quiet` (**6.9%** of idle rolls) against 2 of 103 at `unbearable` (**1.9%**) — **the player who asked for the least Jamal is 3.6 times more likely to get the sad identity material than the player who asked for the most.** (The figures have moved four times and the shape has not: the voice audit found the total stated as 119 when the pool summed to 117 and its two cuts took it to 112; the structural pass took it to 105 by making `idle.09`, `idle.21` and `idle.36` `tail-only`, since a chain target is not in the roll and so is not in the denominator either; and the voice-editor pass took it to 103 by cutting `idle.33` and `idle.38`, which also halved the gated set this paragraph is about. **The ratio moved 3.4 → 3.6 because the quiet pool shrank faster than the total.** It is still an inversion, which is the only part of this paragraph that was ever load-bearing.) Same inversion, smaller, on `low_health.10`–`.13` and `jump_refused.20`, and all seven now carry the gate. Weight could not fix this and neither could a tier; **the arithmetic is why B.4 Q6 was a mechanic question rather than a taste question.**

## attacking

**key:** `attacking`
**split:** gated — `friendly`: `-` | `friendly`. Tagged rows are eligible ONLY when the mod has confirmed friendly-fire damage; when it has, they join the ordinary roll. Never a separate pick. (Spelled with `-` rather than `any` for the untagged rows because this section predates the generalization; the header says they are the same thing)
**fires:** the gun starts shooting, throttled hard so a sustained fight does not turn into a monologue.

Note the deliberate weight on `attacking.03`, the narration row: **book 7 gives him a berserker feeding-frenzy state in which the manners switch off ENTIRELY** — no speech at all, just crunching, whooping and barrel rolls. A wordless attack is more faithful than any line, some of the time, and narration is how the mod says so out loud.

`SUB = friendly` rows should only be eligible when the mod knows he hit something on his own force. If D.5 cannot detect that cheaply, drop the three rows rather than firing them blind — an unprompted apology for damage that did not happen is the one way this pool reads as broken rather than annoying. **Still open, deliberately: B.4 Q11 defers to what the API turns out to provide at D.5/D.7.**

**`attacking.15` was CUT at B.4** (*They will not enjoy Jamal's emissions.*): a flat paraphrase of verbatim `attacking.05` sitting in the same pool, minus *toasty*, which is the entire coinage. Tail of the pool, so no renumber.

**`attacking.14` was CUT at the voice-editor pass and its id is retired.** *Maybe my mouth.* survives at `moving.13`, where `moving.10` asks the question it answers. This pool asks nothing: *Maybe* opening a bubble with no question in front of it is a fragment pointing at nothing, which is Q5's absolute standard (**a player who has never read the books must hit ZERO non-sequiturs**) and the same test that cut `jump_refused.15`. The file's earlier defence — that his mouth is a weapon in both books, so a combat pool gives the fragment a standalone reading — explains why the CONTENT fits and never addressed the *Maybe*. Its own `moving.13` Note said *Non sequitur on purpose*, which is the file writing the defect down and keeping it.

**One consequence, stated because it is a number and not a feeling:** `attacking.14` was the pool's only untagged `unbearable` row, so with friendly fire undetectable **`unbearable` now offers the same 10 distinct strings as `normal`** — the spam tier stops escalating in combat. That is not a floor breach (the floor is four) and it is a sharper version of a risk Q11 already records: if the API cannot report friendly fire, the three `friendly` rows go too and the pool has no `unbearable` material at all. **No filler was written to cover it** — if chotchki wants combat to escalate at `unbearable`, that is a line to WRITE, the same verdict the `platform` and `cooldown` zeroes get.

## damaged

**key:** `damaged`
**split:** none
**fires:** `on_entity_damaged`, throttled to at most one line every N seconds regardless of how much is chewing on him.

**Damage is a NOISE in both books, not a sentence** — hit by a flung mob or a child's spear he YELPS, hit by a thrown wrench he lets out a small wordless shout. Neither book gives him a body complaint at all, only leg complaints. So the verbal slot is spent on leg-quality griping and protest, not on pain, and the noise itself goes to `damaged.02` in the narration channel where it can actually be rendered.

**Two B.4 cuts landed here.** `damaged.08`'s leading *Ow.* is gone (a spelled-out yelp fights the pool's own premise; the protest that followed it survives), and the old `damaged.08` *Jamal did not care for that.* was DROPPED outright rather than rewritten — deadpan understatement is register 4, which fires at catastrophe happening to OTHER people, and everything the row was reaching for is already carried in-register by `damaged.03` (protest), `damaged.09` (hardware denial) and `damaged.10` (lament). The pool was renumbered: old `.09`–`.16` are now `.08`–`.15`.

## low health

**key:** `low_health`
**split:** none — `SUB = sincere` is advisory, see `idle`
**fires:** health ratio crosses a threshold downward (suggest 0.35 and again at 0.15, one line each, not a repeating timer).

**The highest-weight member of this pool is the silence row, and that is the whole point.** Neither book gives him a complaint about his BODY — he complains about legs, never about himself — and in both books his going quiet is how the narration signals real trouble. **A critically-damaged jamaltron that stops talking is more faithful than anything we could write**, so `low_health.01` stays the heaviest row in the file — at weight 12 of the 29 eligible at `quiet` it is **41% of the quiet-tier roll**, which is the number that makes the window below non-negotiable — now as narration that NAMES the silence instead of an absence the player has to infer, and, since the voice audit, one that BUYS the silence it names: 15 s of no speech on that entity (the header carries the requirement).

## jump

**key:** `jump`
**split:** none — `SUB = meta` is an ADVISORY flag for B.4 (fourth wall), not a subpool
**fires:** the jump input is accepted and the arc starts (PLAN E.2). Once per jump, at takeoff.

**THE JUMP IS THE JOKE** (SPEC.md): Jamal is the literal personification of jumping the shark, so this pool knows it is a meta-joke. **B.4 ruled on the fourth wall and split the two rows.** `jump.13` stays: it is literal-minded about the idiom, which keeps it inside his voice — *he* does not get the joke, which is why the row works. `jump.14` (*Watch Jamal be jumped over!*) was CUT: that one is the mod winking at the audience over his head, and nothing else in the file does that. Tail of the pool, so no renumber. `jump.04` moved to the narration channel rather than being cut — see `CH`.

## land

**key:** `land`
**split:** gated — `outcome`: `any` | `held` | `broke`. E.3 must pass the resolved break outcome in; `any` rows always roll, `held` rows only on a clean landing, and `broke` is enumerated-but-empty on purpose (below)
**fires:** the arc resolves and he is back on the ground — **AFTER the leg-break roll has resolved, which is a CHANGE and the reason this section has a sub at all.**

**On legs he lands WELL**, in both books: real leaps landing *deftly*, a midair ballerina twirl that Donut calls elegant, jump-landings used as an offensive attack. So the airborne pose in C.5 should read deliberate and this pool should read pleased with itself. **He is good at this — the book-7 legs just cannot take it twice.** Note that *deftly* is the NARRATION's word for it and it stays there: `land.03` used to launder it into his own mouth as self-assessment and was replaced at the voice audit.

`land.08` is the pool's one narration row, moved there at B.4 rather than cut.

### The fork bug this section used to ship, and the ORDER that fixes it

**The pool fired BEFORE the break roll, so it could only ever guess.** `land.01` *Jamal has landed. Nothing came apart!* (weight 8) and `land.06` *The legs held! Top quality after all.* (weight 5) assert an outcome the mod had not rolled yet — **13 of the 26 weight at `quiet`, in a pool with four strings there.** So on the landing that snaps his legs, a `quiet` player had a coin-flip chance of being told the legs held, and then watching them come apart. That is not a joke landing badly, it is the mod contradicting itself inside one second, at the moment the whole mod exists to deliver.

**The fix is the SEQUENCE, and the sub is the belt on top of it.** Reordering E.3/E.4 so the break roll resolves first is the actual repair; tagging the rows means that a future refactor which quietly restores the old order cannot pick a line that lies. The requirement is written out in the header (*Requirements the catalog cannot enforce*, R1) because the catalog cannot enforce ordering on its own — no column can.

| Sub | Rows | Eligible when |
|---|---|---|
| `held` | `land.01`, `.06`, `.09`, `.11` | the break roll came up clean. All four assert an outcome: *nothing came apart*, *the legs held*, *that was elegant*, *quite pleased with that landing* |
| `any` | the other six | always — they describe the arc, the ground or him, and none of them claims the hardware survived |
| `broke` | **0** | reserved, deliberately unstaffed |

**Why `broke` is empty, stated rather than left to be discovered:** on a break, `legs_break` fires with 21 rows on its `self` fork, and that pool IS the landing line. A second bubble from `land` in the same tick steps on the mod's centerpiece. **The arithmetic says the same thing from the other side** — with `held` gated off, a broken landing leaves `land` two eligible strings at `quiet` (`.02`, `.03`), which is below this file's floor of four. **A pool that thin is a pool that should not be speaking.** So the recommendation to E.3/E.4 is: on a break, `land` says nothing and `legs_break` carries the beat. The `any` rows stay correct-if-fired, which is what makes this safe either way.

## legs break

**key:** `legs_break`
**split:** required — `self` | `external`. The mod already knows whose fault it was, so it always knows which subpool to roll. **Never pick across them.**
**fires:** the break roll succeeds on landing (PLAN E.4) and he swaps to `jamaltron-beached`. Once, at the moment of the break. The apology timer that follows is `flopping`, not this.

**`SUB = self`** — the player pressed jump, so it is HIS doing. He eats it: exclamation → self-narrated blunder in the third person → apology-as-inventory → a formal request for help → and only THEN the unrepentant defense of hopping. Shame is claimed and never acted on. **No quality complaint on this branch, ever.**

**`SUB = external`** — a biter, a train, a rock, anything the player did not order. He does not apologize at all: formal protest to the whole group, a COUNT of how many sets he has been given, and the top-quality grievance. **The one register break in two books used to sit at the bottom of this fork and B.4 CUT it** (old `legs_break.33`, the triple-*Fuck*): no profanity ships, so the portal page needs no content note. It was the pool tail, so nothing renumbered. **The maximum-misery beat now falls to `legs_break.31`** *This was not Jamal's doing.* — the fork's ONLY remaining `unbearable` row, and the closest thing left to a register break, because the grievance there is finally legitimate. (It shipped as *This was not Jamal's doing. For once.* until the voice audit cut the aside: *for once* is a narrator move that needs a self-awareness of his own track record the profile denies him, and it is ruled narration-only at `died.01`. Six plain words at the bottom of the register is what inverted escalation asks for anyway.) Note where the lament weight actually sits though: higher up the pool at `legs_break.28` / `.29` (*Such woe!* / *Such woe I have!*), which is where a player will mostly hear the misery.

**THE FORK DOES NOT END HERE, and until the structural pass it effectively did.** The apology timer that follows is `flopping`, which had no fork awareness at all — so an `external` break announced by `legs_break.25` at `quiet` was being apologized for within one interval. `flopping` now carries the same `self` | `external` split and D.5 must stamp this event's fork on the entity and roll the flop pool with it (**R2** in the header). **Whatever this section decides about fault is a decision about the next ten minutes, not about one bubble.**

The fork matters more than any individual line. Book 7 hands us both branches explicitly; book 8 only ever shows the his-fault branch, which is exactly why it shows no complaint. **When fault is ambiguous, default to `self` and defend the hardware** — he would rather confess cowardice than let anyone conclude his legs failed.

## flopping

**key:** `flopping`
**split:** gated — `fork`: `any` | `self` | `external`, **INHERITED from the `legs_break` event that started the flop, not re-decided per tick.** `any` rows always roll; `self` and `external` rows roll only under the fork the break carried
**fires:** repeating timer while he is `jamaltron-beached` (PLAN E.4), interval scaled by verbosity tier. **The comedic centerpiece of the whole mod** and the only pool designed to be heard dozens of times in a row.

**The punishment is not immobility, it is INDIGNITY.** Freshly wrecked he is slow and pitiful in both books, he complains loudly and continuously while flopping, and he keeps addressing the group as if he were still mid-conversation. The apology spam IS the penalty — so this pool is the biggest in the file and the tier split does real work: at `quiet` he is sympathetic, at `unbearable` he is a war crime. **One row moved channel at the voice audit:** `flopping.23` watches his head-waving from outside, which is the narrator's job and not his — he reports affect as a meter reading, never as observed body language.

### The fork this pool used to erase (D.5 requirement R2)

**`legs_break` splits `self` | `external` and this pool used to delete the distinction within a second.** The external fork is defined by what he does NOT do — *He does not apologize at all* — and `legs_break.25` *Jamal did NOT hop! Jamal wishes this noted.* was promoted to `quiet` for one reason: **so a player who asked for the least Jamal can still tell which break fired.** Then the apology timer starts, `flopping` rolled one undifferentiated pool, and **43% of its ROLLABLE weight — 76 of 178, counted rather than eyeballed — is the apology register.** At that share the chance of getting through three intervals without one is 0.57³ = 19%, so **the fork the mod just spent a `quiet`-tier row announcing is gone within three apology intervals, 81% of the time.** It is not a rare collision, it is the default outcome. (**The figure was 45%, 88 of 194, until the voice-editor pass recomputed it two ways.** The old denominator counted `flopping.21`, a `tail-only` row the picker never rolls, which contradicts the rule this file states everywhere else; and the pass cut `flopping.05` and `flopping.31`. Excluding chain targets is the honest measure, so both numbers moved and the conclusion did not.)

**So `flopping` carries the same fork, and D.5 must roll it with the fork the break event carried.** The fork is a property of the BREAK, not of the tick: it is stamped on the entity at break time, read on every apology tick, and cleared at `repaired`. It rides in the same per-entity `storage` record as `{N}`, the `once_per_save` fired-set and the pending chains, so it costs one more field and no new machinery. **Defaulting rule, inherited from `legs_break` unchanged: when fault is ambiguous, default to `self` and defend the hardware.**

**The classification rule is mechanical on purpose, so a later reader can check it rather than trust it:**

- **`self` (16 rows)** — every row in the APOLOGY register: it says *sorry* / *sorries* / *apology* / *apologizes* / *shame and regret*, or it is one of the apology SHAPES the profile names (the self-narrated *blunder*, the intent disclaimer at `.38`, the take-the-blame confession at `.34`). **No apology-register row is eligible on `external`, and that single sentence is the whole mechanism.** `.18` *I don't see why Jamal shouldn't be able to hop.* is here for the other reason: on an external break he never hopped, so defending the hop is a non sequitur. `.27` *Nothing is wrong.* follows its own `legs_break` assignment (`legs_break.19`, `self`).
- **`external` (4 rows)** — the grievance register: `.06` *Top quality!*, `.14` *And I was led to believe they were top quality.*, `.30` *Set {N} was not top quality either*, and `.26` *Jamal must protest!*. **The `self` fork forbids a quality complaint, ever**, so these four are exactly the rows that must not leak across.
- **`any` (18 rows)** — misery, status readouts, being stuck, asking to be turned over, the rescue request, the narration row. He does these on both forks and splitting them would halve the pool for nothing. `.17` *they are much too small for Jamal!* stays `any` deliberately: it complains about the SPARES on offer, not about the set that broke, and book 7 has him make it on a break that was his own fault.

**Both forks clear the floor, which is the number that decides whether a split is affordable:** `self` runs 6 / 24 / 33 distinct strings by tier, `external` 4 / 17 / 22. **External at `quiet` sits exactly ON the floor of four** — *I do fear I require assistance*, *Such woe!*, *Jamal is stuck!*, *Top quality!* — and that is the right four: no apology anywhere in them, and the one grievance row is the running gag. It is also the tightest spot in the file, so if anything here ever needs a new line, it is that cell.

**Two B.4 cuts, and the pool was renumbered** (old `.38`–`.41` are now `.37`–`.40`):

- **The swear is gone** (old `flopping.42`, the same string as old `legs_break.33`). Pool tail, so it cost no ids. **The maximum-misery beat now falls to `flopping.38`** *It is not Jamal's intention to add any hair-pulling distress.* — not the heaviest row in the pool (the metronome apologies outweigh it several times over) but the DEEPEST one left: it denies INTENT rather than fault, which prices a baseline of distress from him in and claims only the surplus. Bleaker than the swear, and it was already shipping.
- **The old `flopping.37`** *Jamal is not a burden. Jamal is merely horizontal.* **was DROPPED, not rewritten.** It is the best-written original in the file and the furthest out of register: the wit is the WRITER's, about his condition, and he does not do wit about himself. Everything it was carrying — bother-aversion stated flatly, the thing that keeps the player annoyed rather than resentful — is already carried in register by `flopping.37` (formerly `.38`) *Jamal is sorry to be a bother. Jamal is a bother.*, where the joke is that he agrees with the accusation. **Writing a replacement would have been filler; fewer originals beats flat ones.**

## died

**key:** `died`
**split:** none
**fires:** `on_entity_died`. Once, and the player is probably already upset, so the default is mercy.

**He never dies in either book and is explicitly alive after losing his legs in book 8, so the SITUATION is invented no matter what we do here.** Two strings survive as real quotes anyway, and this is worth flagging because the profile's open question #3 says this pool has zero anchor: it does not. *Jamal would get smushed.* is an exact contiguous substring of his own cheerful explanation of how he expects to die, and *Everything will just stop.* is an exact substring of the bk 8 annihilation material. **The lines are verbatim; the event is ours.** **B.4 ruled they SHIP** — a faithful quote fired at a fabricated moment was the call that needed making, and chotchki made it.

`died.01` is the heaviest row on purpose. **Nobody in two books is ever cruel to him, and a joke over the wreck is the mod being cruel to him** — so it is the flattest of the six former silence rows, with no *for once* and no punchline. It reads *Jamal does not get up.* since the voice audit: *Jamal is quiet now.* was the same observation as `low_health.01`, which fires on the way down seconds earlier, and roughly two in three `quiet`-tier deaths printed both. Naming the wreck instead of the silence differentiates them in CONTENT rather than in wording, which is the only kind of difference `GRP` cannot help with. **This pool has a second narration row now** — `died.08`, the *top quality* verdict, which is an epitaph and therefore not an utterance he owns.

## jump refused

**key:** `jump_refused`
**split:** gated — `reason`: `any` | `water` | `blocked` | `platform` | `cooldown` | `autopilot` | `no_driver`. E.2 reports exactly one reason per refusal; `any` rows always roll, a reason-tagged row rolls only on its own reason, and a reason the mod cannot report matches nothing
**fires:** the jump input is rejected — water, a cliff, no valid landing spot, on cooldown, on a space platform (A.6/E.6), under autopilot, or with no driver. E.2 already computes WHICH, and as of B.6 it has to pass it in.

**The best-anchored non-obvious pool in the character**, because book 7 spends a whole argument on being denied the hop and book 8 supplies the flat acceptance that makes the argument funny. The two registers fork cleanly: **he LAMENTS when the parts or the rules insult him, and he ACCEPTS flatly when the geometry simply does not fit.** Both are canon and the flat version is funnier.

Canon cover for the mechanic itself: he is explicitly forbidden from jumping off a tower, with the stated reason that the legs are strong but not THAT strong.

### The reason split (PLAN B.6)

**All 19 rows used to be one undifferentiated pool, which meant the water gag could fire on a cooldown refusal** — a shark refusing to go near water is the best joke in the mod right up until it fires because the player pressed the key twice, at which point it reads as broken rather than funny. `SUB` now carries the REASON, on the `attacking` pool's gated pattern rather than as a hard fork: **a reason-tagged row is eligible only when E.2 reports that exact reason, `any` rows are always eligible, and a reason nothing reports simply never matches.** That last clause is why this lands safely before E.2 exists — an unwired mod reports nothing, every reason-tagged row sits out, and the pool degrades to the `any` rows it already had.

**Staffing is deliberately lopsided, and the honest version of that is a list of zeroes rather than four rows of padding.** Counts are of the 18 surviving rows:

| Reason | Rows | Detection (PLAN E.2) |
|---|---|---|
| `any` | 13 | always eligible — the grievance, the credentials, the flat acceptance. None of them name a cause |
| `water` | 1 — `jump_refused.08` | `tile.prototype.fluid ~= nil`, which is exactly the 6 base water tiles and picks up modded water free |
| `blocked` | 4 — `.11`, `.13`, `.16`, `.17` | `find_non_colliding_position` returns nil: cliffs, buildings, trees |
| `platform` | **0** | Space Age, E.6 forbids it — and E.2 flags it as the one reason whose detection is unconfirmed |
| `cooldown` | **0** | trivial, a tick stamp |
| `autopilot` | **0** | `autopilot_destination` is set |
| `no_driver` | **0** | no driver in the seat |

**The four zeroes are a finding, not an omission.** Nothing in the pool is about being in space, about waiting out a timer, about being under orders, or about an empty driver's seat, and a line written to fill one of those cells would be filler — the thing this file refuses. All four fall through to the `any` pool, which is the correct behaviour and needs no code: they are generic refusals and he has thirteen generic complaints. **Two of them deserve a second look at D.5 rather than a line here:** `no_driver` should probably not speak at all (nobody is in the seat to hear it), and `cooldown` is the one reason a player triggers on purpose, over and over, so it is the likeliest place a repeated generic will wear out. If chotchki wants a platform or cooldown line it has to be WRITTEN — there is nothing in the pool to reassign.

**`water` is one row carrying a whole reason, so it was weighted to actually land.** `jump_refused.08` moved `normal` → `quiet` and 5 → 12, on `legs_break.25`'s argument: a row that tells the player which branch fired is information and has to survive opting out. The generic weight it competes against is 29 at `quiet` and 62 at `normal`, so it takes **29% / 16% / 16%** of a water refusal by tier. That is deliberately not 100%: **there is exactly one water string, and `GRP` anti-repeat suppresses it on a second consecutive water refusal**, so the generic pool has to be able to carry the second lake in a row anyway. **The percentage is the one number in this section worth tuning against a real game at A.7.**

**`blocked` is the sub that pays for itself.** `.16` *I cannot reach!* and `.17` *I am quite snug!* were the two rows a reader could most easily call non-sequiturs — they are the bk 8 wedged-in-a-vehicle beat, reused here. Against a refusal that fired because a cliff or a tree is in the way, *quite snug* stops being a reused fragment and becomes the funniest reading of it, and the two now CHAIN (see below). `.11` *Jamal is too big for that landing* and `.13` *Not here... Mayhaps over there?* are the flat-geometry register the section's own preamble names, and geometry is precisely what `blocked` means.

**`SUB = sincere` is gone from `jump_refused.20`, displaced by `any`.** It was advisory twice over — the header already says a `split: none` generator is correct to ignore it, and what actually makes that row rare is `GATE = once_per_save`, which is untouched. The nine gated rows are enumerated by ID in the header and never depended on this column.

**`jump_refused.15` was CUT, and it leaves a gap.** *It is quite thoroughly gone... Just like his ability to hop.* (the string that lives at `idle.22`). **In `idle` the antecedent is real: the book runs the sense-of-smell sentence, then *Not even one little bit.*, then this line, and `idle.20` → `idle.21` now delivers the first two beats.** In `jump_refused` there is no antecedent and there never can be — the only thing on the table is hopping, which the second clause is COMPARING the referent to, so *It* is either nothing or it is circular. That is the voice audit's own standard (a verbatim line with nothing to point at is still a non-sequitur) applied to a pool boundary instead of a proper noun. **`attacking.14` was held to the same test and survived it**, which is the distinction worth recording: *Maybe my mouth.* has a standalone reading in a combat pool because his mouth is a weapon in both books, and this row has no standalone reading anywhere outside `idle`.

Computed from the tables above, not counted by hand.

**273 rows across 15 sections — 16 pools, since `enter`/`exit` is one section and two — 161 verbatim, 14 adapted, 98 original; 261 speech and 12 narration; median length 38 characters.** Every pool clears the 5–8 minimum; `flopping` and `legs break` carry the load as PLAN E.4 requires, and `idle` is second because it fires on a timer forever. **Four of the sixteen pools now divide further at roll time** — `legs break` by fault, `flopping` by the fault it inherits, `land` by outcome, `jump refused` by refusal reason — so the table below is the honest measure and this one is the inventory.

**Four 2026-09-19 passes cost thirteen rows in total (286 → 273), and exactly one replacement line was written across all four** — `land.03`, at the voice audit, because cutting it would have dropped `land` below the four-distinct-string floor at `quiet`. **The structural pass wrote no new lines at all**, which is the intended shape of a pass whose four jobs are pool DESIGN: it moved one row's trim, re-weighted one row, tagged 69 rows with a condition, wired nine chains and cut one row.

- **The Q5 proper-noun purge cost three** (286 → 283): `idle` 39 → 38, `command_done` 15 → 13.
- **The B.4 rulings cost six** (283 → 277): the swear ×2 rows (Q2), `jump.14` (Q3), and `attacking.15` + two of the *merely* cluster (Q12). `attacking` 15 → 14, `damaged` 16 → 15, `jump` 14 → 13, `legs break` 33 → 32, `flopping` 42 → 40.
- **The structural pass cost one** (274 → 273): `jump_refused.15`, the `idle.22` string in a pool that can never supply its *It*. `jump refused` 19 → 18, and `.15` joins `.18` as a retired id in that pool. **It also re-trimmed `idle.20`**, which changes a shipping string without changing a row count — the only `Line` edit in the pass, made because the old trim orphaned `idle.21`.
- **The voice audit cost three** (277 → 274): `idle.24` / `jump_refused.18` (one string, two rows) and `idle.25`, all referent flips that only a reader of the books could parse. `idle` 38 → 36, `jump refused` 20 → 19. **These are the first cuts to leave GAPS** — the door on renumbering shut before this pass, so `idle.24`, `idle.25` and `jump_refused.18` are retired ids and not free slots.

**No pool crossed the distinct-string floor as a result** — check the table below against the old one: the smallest survivors are `damaged` at `normal` (14 → 13) and `flopping` at `quiet` (8 → 7), both comfortably above the floor of four, and the two pools that sit below it were already there on purpose. The voice audit's cuts took `idle` at `normal` from 29 to 27 and `jump refused` at `unbearable` from 20 to 19, nowhere near the floor — and `land` held at 4 at `quiet` only because `land.03` was REPLACED rather than cut, which is most of the reason it was replaced. **Writing filler to hold a row count is the failure mode this file refuses**, and chotchki's standing rule is the reason: fewer originals beats flat ones.

**But total pool size is the wrong number, because nobody plays at "all three tiers".** Tiers are cumulative, so what a given player actually has is the DISTINCT strings eligible at their setting — and the subpool splits divide their sections on top of that. **Counted the honest way: narration rows count as members, the nine `once_per_save` rows are counted even though a save spends each of them once, and the six `tail-only` chain rows are NOT counted, because the picker never rolls them.**
